criteria.text: `pnpm bench:jev --offline --dir <tmp>` over fixture rows prints one line per `t` in {0.70, 0.80, 0.85, 0.90, 0.95} for `jev` and for `sonnet`, one `none` baseline line, and a final `DECISION:` line. It is tested through `main(argv, deps)` with `deps.fetch` and `deps.exec` that throw when called: neither is called.

On a fixture of 20 rows (5 returned at round 1, 15 approved) where Jev flags the round-1 criterion of 2 of the 5 returned PRs at `pTrue = 0.08` and flags one approved PR at `pTrue = 0.12`: `decide` returns `SHIP` at `t = 0.90`, the lowest `t` with zero clean-PR false positives, with rounds saved at 2/5 = 40%. Moving the approved PR to `pTrue = 0.03` makes it `HOLD (no threshold without false positives)`.
With the same fixture but only 1 of the 5 returned PRs flagged (20% < 25%), `decide` returns `HOLD t=0.90 saved=20%`.
19 usable rows, or 20 rows with 4 round-1 returns, give `INSUFFICIENT DATA` with the right counts. So do rows with `diffAt: "final"` in place of the missing returns.
`metrics` counts a nit-only round-1 gap as met, and counts a flagged criterion that round 1 did not mark unmet as a precision miss, not a round saved.
A row with no Jev answer for criterion 2 is excluded from criterion agreement for criterion 2 and does not raise that PR's false-positive count.
An empty dir prints `DECISION: INSUFFICIENT DATA (rows=0, returned=0)` and exits 0. A dir holding one malformed `.json` exits 1 and names the file.
`parseVerifyBlock` returns the `rounds` array from a PR body holding a `` ```json factory-verify `` block, and `[]` from a body without one (for example PR #259's actual body, pasted into the test).

`collect` with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` unset exits 1 before `deps.fetch` is called. When the stubbed `exec` returns a diff above 32 000 estimated tokens, the written row has `skipped` set and `deps.fetch` was never called.

`decisionRequest` returns a body with `model: "typesafe/jev-1.13"`, `state: {diff, spec}`, and one `criterion:<n>` question per parsed acceptance criterion plus every `CONVENTION_QUESTIONS` entry. `parseDecisions` on a recorded response fixture (the shape #257 fixes) returns `pTrue` per `id` and `usage.cost` as `costUsd`.
No row written by `collect` in the test contains the value of `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (a sentinel string set in the stubbed env).

`build.js`: the `VERDICT` schema accepts an optional integer `criterion` on each gap and still requires `severity, area, location, fix`. Manual step: run `build` on any approved issue. The PR body holds a `factory-verify` json block with one entry per validator round, each with a `headSha` that `git cat-file -e` resolves in the PR's commits. The loop still runs at most 2 rounds with test-verifier before validator, as today.

The docs state that `pnpm bench:jev` exists, that `--offline` makes no network call, the decision rule (lowest threshold with zero clean-PR false positives, ship only if at least 25% of round-1 returns are saved, at least 20 PRs with 5 returns), and that the Jev gate never approves a branch. Checked against `docsText` from `test/docs.ts`. `test/docs-drift.test.ts` does not cover any of this (it covers collectors only).
`pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm test` pass. `scripts/` is already in `tsconfig.json`'s `include`.

Manual: `pnpm bench:jev collect` has run on every merged factory PR whose issue carries a spec comment. The resulting `bench/jev/*.json` rows are committed, and the `--offline` output, including the `DECISION:` line, is posted as a comment on #258.

Part B (second PR, build only if criterion 15's comment reads `DECISION: SHIP t=<t>`):
`JEV_THRESHOLD` in `scripts/jev/questions.ts` equals the `t` from that comment.

`scripts/jev-gate.ts --spec-file <f> --base <branch>`, run in a worktree, prints one JSON object `{ "gaps": [...], "skipped": null | "<reason>" }` and always exits 0. Each gap is `{ severity: "blocker", area, location: "criterion <n>", fix: "<criterion text>" }`. `area` is `"ui"` when the criterion text names a path under `public/` and no path under `src/`, otherwise `"api"`. It is tested through its `main(argv, deps)`: a fetch that rejects, times out (`JEV_TIMEOUT_MS`, 60 000) or returns non-2xx gives `gaps: []` and a `skipped` reason, never a non-zero exit. A missing key does the same.
Only criteria with `1 - pTrue >= JEV_THRESHOLD` become gaps. Convention answers never become gaps.

`build.js` runs the gate once, after the Build phase and before the round loop (phase `Verify`, label `jev #<issue> r0`). A non-empty `gaps` goes to `builder-api`/`builder-ui` through the same fix prompt the loop uses. Then the unchanged loop runs: test-verifier, then validator, max 2 rounds. Round 0 does not count toward the 2. An agent failure or `skipped` logs one line and continues. Jev output never sets `verdict`, and nothing in the gate can make the build reach Release without the validator's `approve`.
The `factory-verify` block gains a `{ "round": 0, "source": "jev", "gaps": [...], "skipped": ... }` entry, so later benchmarks can see what the gate did.
The docs state the gate's threshold value, that a Jev failure or timeout skips the step and never blocks a build, and that the validator still runs after it. Checked against `docsText`.
